A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Seg2Any. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on SACap-Eval, COCO-Stuff and ADE20K, component ablations, qualitative results and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds controlled PLACE-attention comparisons and further qualitative experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same semantic and shape conditioning, contour representation, LoRA adaptation, shape-strength modulation, token filtering and attribute-isolation attention. The new FLUX implementation of PLACE attention is evaluated as a comparator.

E1.justification: v2 adds explicit qualitative coverage of densely crowded, overlapping layouts in Appendix D, Figure 11, including crowds, vehicles and football players. SACap-1M, SACap-Eval, COCO-Stuff and ADE20K remain the training and benchmark datasets; Pix2Cap-COCO appears only in the dataset comparison.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are retained. Appendix C.2 adds a FLUX reimplementation of PLACE attention to comparisons with SAA and SAA+SSFA on all three benchmarks, beyond the original PLACE comparisons already present in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces a controlled comparison using the same FLUX architecture and fixed training settings: 20,000 steps, batch size 16 and learning rate 1e-4. Existing benchmark sizes, resolutions, metrics and main training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds targeted qualitative AIA-removal examples and a matched-backbone SSFA-versus-PLACE analysis with quantitative and visual evidence. Crowded-scene cases are also added, and one Figure 4 example is replaced. These extend the existing component ablations; the computational-cost and scribble-control analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or formal significance tests. The existing computational-cost averaging and minimum/maximum token configurations are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New Tables 5–6 add FLUX PLACE-attention scores, including MIoU 44.56 on COCO-Stuff, 51.56 on ADE20K and class-agnostic MIoU 90.8 on SACap-Eval. Qualitative results are added or replaced. SACap-1M's average mask count changes from 5.7 in v1 Table 5 to 5.9 in v2 Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same instruction definition, attention masks, contour construction, LoRA formulation and guidance-bias mathematics. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: Seg2Any's shape, semantic and attribute control; SACap-1M and SACap-Eval; and claimed state-of-the-art open-set and closed-set performance. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 qualifies CITF's effect from leaving performance unchanged or unaffected to almost unchanged or marginally affected. Broader Impacts changes the proposed applications to controllable image generation, video generation and segmentation-dataset construction. The resource and annotation-noise limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 documents PLACE attention's FLUX reimplementation and its training settings, including four H100 GPUs. This supplies reproducibility information for the added comparison. Existing Seg2Any implementation details, annotation instructions and the project link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Groundit, CreatiDesign, UniGen, SimpleAR, Pix2Cap-COCO and application-related generation work. The dense-caption dataset comparison adds Pix2Cap-COCO. These are limited extensions; the positioning relative to OminiControl, EliGen and masked-attention approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. v2 expands affiliations, adds an acknowledgment, makes localized wording edits and inserts an ablation appendix. The dataset appendix moves from C to E, placing the qualitative-results section before it.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6 and Figures 8, 9 and 11, replaces Figure 4's fourth example column and adds a dataset-table row. Existing tables and appendix figures are relocated or renumbered, while their visual formats and the main framework diagram are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The matched-FLUX comparison in Appendix C.2 improves attribution of SSFA's benefits, and the additional qualitative ablations strengthen supporting evidence. Correcting the dataset average and qualifying CITF's performance effect improve accuracy. The main results remain unchanged, and the new comparison supports shape accuracy while remaining mixed on other quality metrics, so the overall improvement is limited.
